calls.title: Annual firm volume versus pilot and purchase quantities

turns.speaker: PROSPECT
turns.text: Our existing firm prepares 1,260 returns annually: 1,020 personal and 240 business.

turns.speaker: ROSS
turns.text: How many completed returns would you want to use in an evaluation of our product?

turns.speaker: PROSPECT
turns.text: Twelve completed returns.

turns.speaker: ROSS
turns.text: How should we split that evaluation sample?

turns.speaker: PROSPECT
turns.text: Eight personal and four business overall, all already completed so we can compare to known results.

turns.speaker: ROSS
turns.text: And if the evaluation works, what would your initial annual purchase of our product look like?

turns.speaker: PROSPECT
turns.text: For the existing firm, 180 returns is our planning target for a first year.

turns.speaker: PROSPECT
turns.text: That is how many we might process with you, not our whole annual practice volume.

turns.speaker: PROSPECT
turns.text: I checked our final annual totals: actually 1,280 firm returns, including 1,040 personal and 240 business.
